# HiveGate

> Open-source FastAPI service that runs [Agno](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno) agents as a production REST API. MIT-licensed. It adds what serving agents to many users needs: per-user sessions, per-user OAuth tokens for Google and Microsoft, human approval before risky tool calls, agents/prompts/skills managed as data through the API, per-tenant knowledge on Qdrant, multi-agent teams with a supervisor and containerized workers, MCP tools over Streamable HTTP, token usage and cost metering, and tracing. One-click deploy to Render, Railway and Koyeb from the prebuilt image `ghcr.io/hivegate-ai/hivegate:latest`.

HiveGate is not a request-routing API gateway like Kong; it runs AI agents and exposes them over HTTP. If your agents are defined in code and Agno's own AgentOS covers your needs, use AgentOS.

Every docs page and blog post is also served as plain markdown at the same URL with `.md` (for example https://hivegate.dev/docs/quickstart.md); the full corpus is in [llms-full.txt](https://hivegate.dev/llms-full.txt).

## Site
- [Landing page](https://hivegate.dev/): tagline, features, deploy buttons, quickstart
- [Docs](https://hivegate.dev/docs/): architecture diagram, API reference, configuration, toolkits, supervisor platform, database schema, observability
- [Deploy guide](https://hivegate.dev/deploy/): one-click platforms, Kubernetes, cloud-specific manifests, smoke test, operational notes
- [Blog](https://hivegate.dev/blog/): practical write-ups with real endpoints and snippets

## Blog
- [Deploying Agno agents to production as a REST API](https://hivegate.dev/blog/deploy-agno-agents-production-rest-api/): per-user sessions, Postgres-backed history, API keys, streaming, one-click Docker deploy, and when Agno's AgentOS is enough
- [Per-user Google and Microsoft OAuth for AI agents](https://hivegate.dev/blog/per-user-google-microsoft-oauth-ai-agents/): storing each user's tokens encrypted, automatic refresh, and how the Gmail, Outlook, Calendar, Contacts and Drive toolkits use them
- [Human approval before risky agent tool calls](https://hivegate.dev/blog/human-approval-agent-tool-calls/): how a run pauses on a write tool, approving, editing or denying it through the commit API, and what is recorded
- [LLM token usage and cost tracking per user and tenant](https://hivegate.dev/blog/llm-token-usage-cost-tracking/): the token_usage row behind every model call, the /usage API by user, tenant and agent, how prices are applied, and Claude prompt caching
- [Claude prompt caching for agents: what breaks the cache](https://hivegate.dev/blog/claude-prompt-caching-agents/): how cache breakpoints work for Agno agents, why a timestamp or per-user value in the system prompt stops cross-run cache hits, and how to check the hit rate with /usage

## Source
- [Repository (app)](https://github.com/hivegate-ai/hivegate): FastAPI + Agno service, Python 3.11+, MIT. Its README is the most current reference, including the `/usage` cost API and prompt caching
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/hivegate-ai/hivegate/issues/72): what's planned next (per-user MCP authentication, approval gates for MCP tools)
- [Repository (deploy)](https://github.com/hivegate-ai/deploy): one-click platform configs, K8s manifests, build pipeline
- [Container image](https://github.com/hivegate-ai/hivegate/pkgs/container/hivegate): multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) at `ghcr.io/hivegate-ai/hivegate`
